Hosts can file it free on the state portal (kbs.egm.gov.tr, Jandarma KBS Tesis 2), and cheap KBS tools for hotels and pensions already exist (LKBS, 3T Kimbil, Kimlik Bildirim 2007). The permit is a one-off e-Devlet application. Under circular 2026/4, platforms check permit numbers through the ministry API, and tax is the accountant's job. I found no villa or channel-manager product with KBS integration (searched HotelRunner, Elektraweb, Klik.villas, Hostaway). Market size is unsettled: no national permit count found; one report cites about 16k applicants in Kaş, Kalkan and Fethiye alone.

result.killer: No named killer. Not settled: whether the Bilgi Sistemi will have an API and how much it will check by itself; this can't be known until it launches (planned for 1 Jan 2027).
result.reason: I found no product that kills this outright. No rental software, consultancy or association tool (TOKKDER, AKKON) mentions the yetki belgesi or the new Bilgi Sistemi. The permit is a one-off filing issued free through the Ministry's Bilgi Sistemi, which also registers vehicles and checks them for marketplaces, so the state tool may do the core job. What recurs is light: fleet age (6 years), km (180k/300k), muayene and insurance checks, and deposit caps. Existing rental software, already tied to the police KABİS system, can add those. The 5-vehicle (10 in big metro districts) minimum will push the smallest esnaf out. No small-firm exemption. No API, operator count, fines or renewal period published yet.

result.killer: This duty is not new for the buyers named in the claim. Domestic carriers' trucks and buses have had to use digital tachographs since a 2012 rule change. Since 31/12/2019 a Ministry of Transport rule has required them to download that data and send it to the ministry (Webtekno, 3 Jan 2020). Drivers must also send their card data to STAUM, the TOBB-run tachograph centre. So K1/L1 hauliers and bus firms are already served by an established vendor market: Mobiliz Tachowise, Seyir Mobil, Teltonika TachoSync, a Turkish-built cable-plus-archive tool, and local tachograph workshops. Law 7574 also says records will be transferred to a state database that police and the Labour Ministry can audit, so the state already handles the upload channel.
result.reason: The claim treats Law 7574 as a new tachograph and data duty for small hauliers and bus firms. In fact, download and sending data to the ministry has been compulsory for buses and trucks since end-2019. About 1.06 million vehicles were reported to fall under the digital tachograph rules, and several vendors already serve them. Law 7574 mainly moves the duty into the traffic law with police fines and model-year deadlines, and it routes records to a state database. The new buyers are vehicles outside the old transport-licence rules, a smaller and unclear group. NTV and the police (EGM) say it applies only to newly registered vehicles, which conflicts with the phase-in table in the law. The implementing regulation (due Feb 2027) was not found. There is still room for a cheaper done-for-you service, but the duty is not new and the market is not empty.

coverage.category: 36. Car and vehicle rental firms: new Motorlu Kara Taşıtlarının Kiralanması Hakkında Yönetmelik (RG 15 Aug 2026)
coverage.found: Takes effect 1 Jan 2027. Existing firms must hold a yetki belgesi by 1 Jul 2027, and the fleet, age and km requirements apply from 1 Jan 2028. The Ministry may extend each by up to a year. Belge per business and per branch, issued by the ticaret il müdürlüğü through a Motorlu Kara Taşıtı Kiralama Bilgi Sistemi that the Ministry must build by 1 Jan 2027. Minimum fleet 10 (metro districts over 30k) or 5, with some in the firm's name. Vehicles at most 6 model-years old, under 180k km (300k for EV), with no heavy-damage record, valid muayene and traffic insurance. A Seviye 4 'kiralama danışmanı' vocational certificate is needed for the responsible person. Deposit caps of 3 days (up to 6-day rentals) or 7 days (7-29 days), refund within 7 days, an independent expert report for damage charges, contract records kept 5 years, and marketplaces must verify the belge. Fines under Laws 6563 and 6585. Not found: renewal period and teminat.

result.duty:
Real and in the law. The Motorlu Kara Taşıtlarının Kiralanması Hakkında Yönetmelik (Ministry of Trade regulation on motor vehicle rental) was published in Resmî Gazete 33341 on 15 Aug 2026 and takes effect on 1 Jan 2027. It covers merchants and esnaf (small tradespeople) who rent vehicles to consumers on short-term rentals. Rentals of 30 days or more, car sharing and camper rentals are excluded.

Key requirements:
- A yetki belgesi (operating permit) for each business and each branch. It is issued by the provincial trade directorate through the Motorlu Kara Taşıtı Kiralama Bilgi Sistemi, the Ministry's online system, which must be built by 1 Jan 2027.
- Every rental vehicle must be registered in that system.
- Existing firms must get the permit by 1 Jul 2027.
- Minimum fleet, vehicle age (6 years), mileage (180k km, or 300k km for electric) and safety rules apply to existing firms from 1 Jan 2028. The Ministry can extend these deadlines by up to one year.
- Minimum fleet: 10 vehicles in metropolitan districts over 30k population (at least 5 registered in the firm's name, and at least 2 hybrid or electric). Elsewhere: 5 vehicles (at least 2 in the firm's name).
- The kiralama sorumlusu (person responsible for rentals) must hold a Seviye 4 (Level 4) vocational certificate.
- Rental contracts must be kept for 5 years.
- Cheques, promissory notes and guarantee letters may not be taken as deposits. Several outlets report a 7-day deposit refund deadline, which I did not confirm in the final text.
- From 1 Jan 2028, listing platforms must check the permit before publishing a listing.

Penalties are administrative fines under Laws 6563 and 6585; no amounts were found. Permit validity and renewal periods were not found. Every source I read was secondary; I did not open the Resmî Gazete text itself. Much of the work is a one-off application plus keeping the fleet up to date in a free state system.
result.market: Sector representatives quoted in the press say roughly 1,500 to 2,000 short-term rental firms appear in official records, while trade chambers have about 15,000 to 16,000 businesses registered with rental activity. Many of those are side businesses (for example markets or barbers), which the regulation pushes out because only dedicated rental firms may rent. A realistic target is perhaps 2,000 to 6,000 dedicated small firms. This is an estimate; no official register count was found.
result.reason: The duty is real, the deadlines are fixed and nothing commercial covers it yet. But the core filing (permit application and vehicle registration) runs through a free Ministry system that should be live by Jan 2027. What is left to automate is mostly a one-off permit project plus light fleet checks (age, mileage, minimum fleet mix, deposits) that existing rental software vendors can add cheaply. Recurring pain after 2027 is low, apart from keeping the fleet list current. The market is small and shrinking: about 2,000 formal firms, with many side-business renters leaving. A done-for-you service for permit and Seviye 4 certificate preparation before July 2027 could sell, but it is a short window. Fine amounts, renewal period and API availability are still unknown.

Duty: the maintenance contract is mandatory, the periyodik kontrol is done by A-type bodies, and administrative fines apply under the 2025 amendment. The regulation was split into two, so the old 2015 text is repealed, and the colour label rules were not confirmed from a primary source. Market: about 477k lifts in 2016 and about 2.8k to 3.1k firms with CE or HYB certificates, per an old EMO document. Small maintenance firms are accessible, but the market is crowded and the ATS state system exists.

result.reason: Duty is real: Work Equipment Regulation amended 23 Dec 2025 (RG 33116). Periodic control applies only to Annex-III equipment, usually yearly for forklifts and air tanks. The İSG-KATİP contract is signed between employer and inspector at least 1 day before the inspection. The official EKİPNET module sits inside İSG-KATİP. Penalties fall mainly on the authorized inspector, not the owner. Competition could not be settled. Three Turkish searches found no reminder-only product, but also no vendor survey. The OSGB, CMMS and inspection-firm reminder question is open. The market count is not found. Likely buyers are small, low-willingness-to-pay, and the inspector or OSGB already books the inspection. The score stays at 3.

The duty exists: households must register each day worked for under-10-day domestic workers through e-Devlet, and the Cott Group page matches the claim. I found no current fine amount for this regime. The same-day rule comes from a practice guide, not statute, so it is not firmly sourced. The e-Devlet screens and the older SMS route (5510) already do the filing. A 2017 Webrazzi article shows Temizlikyolda, a cleaning platform, integrated the SMS system, so a partial competitor exists. I found no dedicated reminder app. Searches were only 2, and I opened no pages; the search summaries relied on mostly old news (2016-2019). The market is a large number of households, but each files only a few days a month, so willingness to pay is weak. A reminder is a thin feature and the buyer is hard to reach. The premium helper adds little beyond a free state calculator.

The duty is real. Circular 2026/4 (14 Aug 2026) bars electronic marketing or sale without one of four permit types. It requires full removal of flagged listings and urgent integration of the Ministry's verification API. Penalties are only "administrative sanctions", with no amounts, and no calendar deadline. The API is a free state tool with public docs (Basic auth, GET /document-list, POST /publication-notifications). It is aimed at platforms and agencies' own software, so the buyers are mainly software vendors, channel managers and OTAs that build it in-house. Small agencies rarely list property, and I found no competitor product. The buyer count was not verified: roughly 7,000 agencies is an undated, probably old figure. The market is thin, it is a one-off integration, and willingness to pay is low. Only a niche, such as a middleware or connector for small channel managers, is plausible.

The EUDR (Reg. 2023/1115) is EU law, not Turkish law. It reaches Turkish firms only through EU buyers' data requests. Amending Reg. 2025/2650 (in force 26 Dec 2025) sets application at 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium operators and for micro/small firms already under the EU Timber Regulation, and 30 Jun 2027 for other micro/small firms. The Commission ruled out further delay. The simplification cuts the duty: downstream operators and traders only collect and keep references, and micro/small primary operators file a one-off declaration. Turkey's low-risk classification is only in a law-firm source; I did not check it against the EU act. Global vendors cover the job (Tracextech, Sourcemap, osapiens, Trustrace); I found no Turkish SME product. The Turkish market is not sized, and no per-firm count was found. The duty is weak and indirect, with global competition and a diffuse buyer.

The KOOPBİS duty is real. The Kooperatif Bilgi Sistemi Yönetmeliği requires document upload before the general assembly and a general-assembly record within 5 working days after it. The data-load deadline was 26 Apr 2026. Late or missing uploads can expose board members to penalties, per a search summary. The fetched alomaliye article gave no penalty or liability text, so the personal-liability claim is unverified. I found no commercial co-op software, but the state portal covers the filing itself. Market: 49,475 co-operatives are registered, but only about 9,900 are active (Nov 2025), and the Trade Ministry covers 11,660. Volunteer boards pay little, and the one-off load is over. I found no housing or agricultural split. The score is low because of the small active base, low willingness to pay and a thin recurring job.

result.reason: The duties are real. Used-car dealers are obliged parties under Law 5549 art. 2 and the Measures Regulation art. 4. They must identify customers, check beneficial owners, report suspicious transactions within 10 business days, and keep records 8 years. The page also gives an identification threshold of 370,000 TL, updated Oct 2026. The Ministry of Trade authorisation certificate is mandatory, with 84,804 certificates issued cumulatively (June 2026) and 305m TL in fines for trading without one. EİDS verification applies to listings. The Dec 2025 amendment moved the deadlines to 1 Apr 2026 and 1 Jul 2026. Stock programs (LUQU, Hursoft, ProGaleri) show no MASAK or EİDS features. Weaknesses: MASAK dealer duties are mostly per-sale paperwork with no recurring filing, and the notary also identifies the parties. The page gives no fine amounts. Dealers are a low-spend, fragmented segment. Not checked: the MASAK Online filing format, the status of the 6-month/6,000 km rule after 1 Jul 2026, and dealer ERP vendors beyond the three above.
